source.title: Progressive Transfer Learning for Person Re-identification
source.authors: Zhengxu Yu; Zhong-Ming Jin; Long Wei; Jishun Guo; Jian-Qiang Huang; Deng Cai; Xiao-Fei He; Xian-Sheng Hua

record.tranche_reason: Compares large and smaller batch settings in person re-identification fine-tuning and reports held-out performance, extending batch-size findings to a new setting.
record.gate_note: The paper reports the batch-size comparison in Table II and explicitly says the large batch resulted in poor performance. Other PTL results do not test the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study compares held-out performance at two batch sizes under the same stated 50-epoch fine-tuning budget, testing V5 in person re-identification.
record.authors_conclusion: The recorded batch-size conclusion is accurate: the authors say increasing batch size did not effectively address the mini-batch/dataset distribution mismatch and produced poorer performance. Their overall conclusion is that PTL and its variants improve backbone performance on person re-identification and image-classification benchmarks.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares batch sizes during person re-identification fine-tuning, rather than testing the original generalization-gap settings and measures.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size: DenseNet-161* uses 90, while DenseNet-161 uses 32.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 3 qualitatively depicts a wider loss landscape for DenseNet-100+PTL-v2 than DenseNet-100 on CIFAR-100; Table VII reports lower test error for the modified model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: PTL-v2 produces a visually wider loss landscape alongside improved test performance. This does not establish V7's magnitude-aware sharpness–generalization-gap relationship or comparative ranking of measures.

record.peer_reviewed: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
record.problems: The batch-size comparison is reported for one dataset and model family; the two listed settings have no reported uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported results directly test the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width increases beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizers under different tuning budgets.
Image-classification and language-model batch comparisons; workload-dependent thresholds; recovery through longer training, learning-rate scaling, warmup, normalization or regularization changes.
Dropout effects across training-set sizes and regularization settings.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, measured generalization gaps at similarly low training loss, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal of highly memorized examples compared with random removal.

record.verdict_notes: A new task setting is not itself evidence requiring a limits_scope label. The batch comparison reports no uncertainty estimates or training performance, and does not establish a sharp-minimum mechanism.

versions.untested_parts: Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Image-classification and language-model settings; workload-dependent batch thresholds; training/test error gap; adaptations such as longer training, warmup, normalization, and regularization.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: DenseNet-161*
rows.note: The paper identifies DenseNet-161* as using batch size 90 and DenseNet-161 as using batch size 32; it states that the large batch resulted in poor performance.
rows.check: The numbers and conditions are correct, but the state is inverted: mAP falls from 76.40 to 69.90 when batch size increases from 32 to 90, as V5 predicts.

rows.subject: DenseNet-161*
rows.note: The paper identifies DenseNet-161* as using batch size 90 and DenseNet-161 as using batch size 32; it states that the large batch resulted in poor performance.
rows.check: The numbers and conditions are correct, but the state is inverted: CMC-1 falls from 91.70 to 88.30 when batch size increases from 32 to 90, as V5 predicts.

relationships.condition: ImageNet-pretrained DenseNet-161 fine-tuned on Market-1501 for 50 epochs, batch size 90 versus 32.
relationships.reason: R1 and R2 show lower held-out mAP (69.90 versus 76.40) and CMC-1 (88.30 versus 91.70) with the larger batch, extending the predicted penalty to person re-identification.
relationships.display_finding: Unverified results suggest that the larger batch reduced both held-out mean average precision (mAP) and rank-1 cumulative matching accuracy (CMC-1).

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The batch-90 model has lower mAP and CMC-1 than the batch-32 model, but this is a person re-identification setting rather than the version's image-classification or language-model benchmarks (R1, R2).
